security_audit.summary: The pipe-to-shell installer and command-substitution download flow are confirmed risks because they execute or install remote content. Most API key, shell completion, path traversal, and documentation URL findings are false positives. Additional concerns are automatic local file upload and Twitter/X account automation.

remediation.issue: Remote installer is piped directly to sh.
remediation.suggestion: Replace curl-to-shell setup with a verified package manager path or a signed manual download flow.

remediation.issue: Manual install uses command substitution from a remote manifest.
remediation.suggestion: Use explicit platform download URLs and verify checksums before extraction or installation.

remediation.issue: Local paths can be uploaded to cloud apps.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit confirmation before uploading any local file path or home-directory path.

remediation.issue: Twitter/X actions can change external account state.
remediation.suggestion: Require user approval before posting, messaging, following, liking, or retweeting.

remediation.issue: Additional skills are installed through npx commands.
remediation.suggestion: Pin dependency sources and document the exact trust boundary for related skill installation.

semantic_findings.title: Automatic Local File Uploads to Cloud Apps
semantic_findings.description: The skill states that local file paths are automatically uploaded when an app input accepts a URL. This can expose user files if an agent supplies paths without explicit confirmation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The behavior is explicitly documented in both the main skill and running-apps reference. The risk is contextual data exposure, not just filesystem access.

semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The listed examples and categories explicitly include account-changing Twitter/X actions. Legitimate use is possible, but the side effects require confirmation controls.

content.user_title: Run inference.sh AI Apps from the CLI
content.value_statement: Teams need a consistent way to run many cloud AI apps from one terminal. This skill gives CLI commands for discovery, inputs, execution, and task tracking.
actual_capabilities: Shows installation, login, update, and API key setup for the belt CLI.
Lists, searches, filters, and inspects inference.sh apps from the command line.
Runs apps with inline input, saved input files, or no-wait task submission.
Tracks task status and saves generated results for later use.
Explains local file uploads for image, video, audio, and media workflows.
Covers image, video, LLM, search, 3D, utility, and Twitter/X app categories.
limitations: Requires an inference.sh account, available credits, and the belt CLI.
Runs cloud apps, so results depend on external service availability.
Local file paths can upload files to inference.sh services.
Does not implement model logic or replace each app schema.

use_cases.title: Prototype AI media workflows
use_cases.description: Generate sample inputs, run image or video apps, and track task results from one terminal workflow.

use_cases.title: Explore available cloud models
use_cases.description: Search the public app store, compare app details, and choose models for a project.

use_cases.title: Automate repeatable AI tasks
use_cases.description: Run saved inputs, submit long jobs without waiting, and retrieve outputs when tasks complete.

prompt_templates.title: Find apps for a task
prompt_templates.prompt: Find inference.sh apps for image generation. Show the best app names and the next command I should run.

prompt_templates.title: Create a sample run
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create sample input for a FLUX image app, run it, and explain where the result will appear.

prompt_templates.title: Track a long video job
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a Veo video app without waiting, then show how to check task status and save the final result.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a multi-app workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a repeatable workflow that searches for an app, prepares input, runs it, and stores outputs safely.

best_practices: Review each app schema before preparing inputs or uploading files.
Confirm local file uploads and account actions before running commands.
Use saved input files for repeatable jobs and easier review.
anti_patterns: Do not pipe remote installers to a shell without independent verification.
Do not pass sensitive local paths unless the upload is required.
Do not automate Twitter/X actions without explicit account-owner approval.

faq.question: What does this skill help me do?
faq.answer: It helps you discover, run, and track inference.sh apps through the belt CLI.

faq.question: Do I need an inference.sh account?
faq.answer: Yes. Authentication is required before running apps or using account-specific commands.

faq.question: Can it run image and video models?
faq.answer: Yes. The references include FLUX, Veo, Seedance, Wan, and other media apps.

faq.question: Can it upload local files?
faq.answer: Yes. The CLI can upload local paths when an app input accepts media.

faq.question: Does it support long-running tasks?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows no-wait execution, task status checks, and result saving.

faq.question: What should I review before using it?
faq.answer: Review installer safety, app permissions, local file paths, API keys, and account-changing actions.
